key_decisions.decision: Keeps her proposed care and bodily proximity without turning the plan into a stated marriage.
Makes the knowing idiom explicit while retaining the narrator’s distinction between care and intercourse.
Keeps self-exaltation and the display that echoes Absalom, with horsemen as stated here.
Preserves David’s failure to challenge, beauty, and birth order without making the two sons share a mother.
Keeps Nathan’s urgent report and David’s lack of knowledge.
Preserves the threatened lives as Nathan’s warning without inventing an already issued death order.
Keeps the proposed speech and its appeal to an oath not previously narrated.
Preserves Bathsheba’s actual version of the reported oath, including the divine name.
Keeps the direct contrast between the rival’s action and David’s ignorance.
Retains her particular list rather than replacing it with Nathan’s or the narrator’s.
Retains the ancestral death idiom and the political danger of being counted guilty.
Reads the contextually interrogative speech without turning it into an assertion that David authorized Adonijah.
Keeps Nathan’s distinct guest list and the reported acclamation.
Preserves all four excluded persons in Nathan’s account.
Follows read singular your servant rather than written plural.
Keeps the emphatic today and David’s explicit confirmation of the oath.
Keeps both commissioned figures, anointing, and the prescribed acclamation.
Keeps Amen and the wish for divine confirmation rather than declaring it already spoken.
Keeps Zadok as the actual anointer named here and distinguishes the oil horn from the signal horn.
Preserves the exuberant earth-splitting image without making a separate geological report.
Retains the mistaken good-man/good-news inference that echoes the runners in 2 Samuel.
Keeps Jonathan’s joint attribution rather than harmonizing it with the narrator’s singular anointer in verse 39.
Follows read God rather than your God and keeps name and throne comparisons.
Retains the refuge gesture without assuming it guarantees protection.
Keeps the requested oath and explicit feared execution.
Preserves conditional clemency rather than converting it into the unconditional oath requested.
